22274-julia-and-her-romeo-a-chronicle-of:
Julia and Her Romeo is a chronicle of Castle Barfield from David Christie Murray's Schwartz. Murray opens in 1820, when Abel Reddy farmed his own land at Perry Hall End. The two great houses of the parish were built as far apart as their boundaries allowed. Their owners, the Reddys and the Mountains, were a sort of Capulets and Montagues, hating each other for generations.

Samson and Abel kept the ancient grudge in full force. Into that feud Murray sets Julia and her Romeo, young lovers on opposite sides. Shakespeare's pattern is worn openly and kindly. The tale is village romance with a feud for its engine, told in Murray's easy style.

Director Oliver Stone talks with Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, about the cover-up he sees behind the JFK assassination. Stone's film JFK made him the most famous voice of the case for a generation. Decades later, he has not moved from his ground.

He lays out the points he trusts: the wounds, the witnesses, and the files still held back. Rogan asks why the story will not die and what full disclosure would change. The segment is a veteran storyteller's brief for the idea that the public was never told the whole truth about Dallas.
